upsertPapers.title: Improved Sublinear Algorithms for Classical and Quantum Graph Coloring
upsertPapers.versionNote: The HTML displays arXiv:2502.06024v1 (9 February 2025) and an internal manuscript date of 24 August 2026. The abstract history lists only v1; no later revision number is asserted.

upsertSlices.label: Adjacency list neighbor queries only
assumptions: All n vertices are known, including isolates; lists are consistent with one simple undirected graph.
The oracle returns ⊥ after the end of each finite list. A padded list that never signals termination is a different model.
No degree or pair queries are used. The implementation does not need Δ in advance.
The exact count describes this full-scan implementation, not every coloring algorithm and not a query lower bound.
When m=0, the scan still makes n end tests and outputs n copies of color 1. For Δ≥1, n+2m≤n(Δ+1)≤2nΔ.

xAxis.label: Number of colors q · symbolic palette

yAxis.label: Neighbor calls Q · exact implementation cost
yAxis.note: One symbolic formula for an implemented upper bound; no numerical exponent, feasibility region or lower-bound shading.

parameters.n: Known vertex count, n≥1, including isolates
parameters.Delta: Maximum degree; not required as input by greedy
parameters.coordinateConvention: Symbolic exact scan n+2m paired with Δ+1 colors. No forced quadratic exponent.

results.bound: Exactly n+2m neighbor calls for the scan-and-greedy implementation
results.guarantee: Proper vertex coloring from the common palette [Δ+1]; Deterministic; correct on every input satisfying the graph and oracle promises.
results.sourceLocation: §1 query-model definition and greedy baseline; Table 1 and the g(Δ)=nΔ discussion before Corollary 2
results.notes: The exact scan formula and RAM implementation are elementary atlas derivations from the source's access definition and greedy baseline. They are not a new author-stated optimality theorem. Sparse graphs can have high Δ, so m is retained instead of plotting every instance at n². Source coarse baseline: O(nΔ) for Δ≥1. Total RAM time O(n+m); output n assignments.
